page.text:
A set is termed *nonempty* if it contains at least one element. In
mathematical analysis and abstract algebra, nonemptiness is often an
indispensable hypothesis: choice functions cannot select from empty sets,
maximal elements require nonempty partially ordered sets, and sub-
structures must contain identity elements.
